title: Redesign StrokeSculpt.apply, an 810-line method at the JIT size limit
user-messages: can we make a ticket ot fix all of the frictions we are finding
description:
Follow-up from MESH-80. StrokeSculpt.apply is one method of about 810 lines and 7,973 bytes of bytecode, 27 bytes under HotSpot's 8,000-byte HugeMethodLimit past which the JIT never compiles it (a skull pass then runs about ten times slower). MESH-80 had to reorganise code to stay under it (shared nearestDistances, merged offset and relax loops), and MESH-78's fold prevention lands in the same method. The user's rule: a method over about 150 lines means rethinking the design, not splitting into single-caller helpers.

Why it is its own ticket: the redesign (stroke parsing and mirror copies, adaptive refinement, per-stroke displacement fields, relax and symmetrise as named concepts each with more than one user) touches every line MESH-78 is changing; do it after MESH-78 lands, with StrokeSculptTest and the sample DSLs' captures unchanged.
definition-of-done: 1. No StrokeSculpt method over about 150 lines, every concept with more than one user, StrokeSculptTest and sample captures unchanged, a skull pass no slower.
testing-plan: 1. StrokeSculptTest; 2. capture the stroke-sculpt samples before/after; 3. javap sizes.
changes-made: Superseded by MESH-86, whose DoD required StrokeSculpt.apply to stop being one 800-line method: apply is now a 90-line orchestrator (1,006 bytecode bytes) over SculptStroke/ChainStroke/FillStroke/SilhouetteStroke, StrokeRefinement, MidpointSplit and DisplacementSum, StrokeSculptTest unchanged and passing. Close this when MESH-86 lands; MESH-78's unfold goes on the summed pass's final step.
